transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-02-14
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (HelioWorks ML), Dana Lee (HelioWorks CTO), Marta Ruiz (HelioWorks SRE)

Summary (auto): Quick Optimize walkthrough focusing on INT8/FP8 quantization profiles. Showed quality vs latency charts, demo of 4k/8k token runs, discussed PoC scope and security questions.

[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll dive into the Optimize quant profiles — I think Priya will run the demo and I'll cover customer questions and next steps.
[00:18] Priya Shah: cool, hi all. So quick agenda: background + why quantization matters, INT8 vs FP8 tradeoffs, demo of latency/quality, then recommendations and PoC plan.
[00:35] Samir Patel: sounds good. our primary goal is to reduce token cost and keep latency under 120ms for 512-token prompts; accuracy tolerance is small for some of our generative summarization routes.
[00:48] Dana Lee: and from infra side we need SSO and VPC setup; we may go Dedicated if latency hits matter.
[00:57] Priya Shah: noted. quick caveat — transcribed names may be a bit off in the export.

[01:05] Priya: So first, why quantization — in RedwoodOptimize we generate profiles that pick per-layer scaling and quant types so you can run INT8 or FP8. INT8 generally gives the biggest memory reduction, often ~2x model size versus FP16, while FP8 keeps more dynamic range and often preserves quality better.
[01:30] Samir: rough rule of thumb numbers — what latency delta should we expect switching from FP16 to INT8 or FP8?
[01:40] Priya: On GPU families we've benchmarked, INT8 can reduce inference latency ~20-35% for autoregressive decoding depending on sequence length and kernel coverage; FP8 usually gives ~10-20% improvement but with fewer quality regressions. But these numbers vary by model and batch.
[02:05] Marta Ruiz: are those numbers for single-request latency or throughput? we care about p95 single-shot latencies for interactivity.
[02:12] Priya: good call — those were median token throughput numbers for continuous batching scenarios. For single-request p95 at 512 tokens, INT8 reductions are still visible but sometimes smaller; e.g., we saw 15% p95 win on T4-class setups, 25-30% on newer Ampere/Blackwell, hardware dependent.

[02:35] Alex: and remember Redwood has automatic fallback and rollouts — you can start traffic on INT8 and if quality drifts commit traffic to FP8 or FP16 automatically. Priya will show the Optimize UI where we tie this to evals.

[02:50] Priya: switching to demo — I'm sharing my screen. (brief pause) okay I have an 8k token run we prepared — first with FP16 baseline, then FP8 profile, then INT8 profile. note: transcription may show "eight k" weirdly.

[03:20] [03:20] Priya (demo): Baseline FP16: p50 latency 180ms per token, end-to-end 8k generation took X (demo shows ~14.3s), quality score (automated rouge-like eval on our prompt set) is 0.92.
[03:45] Priya: FP8 profile: we kept higher precision for attention heads, quantized feedforward to FP8 — latency improved to p50 145ms per token, total 12.1s, quality dropped to 0.90 (small drop).
[04:05] Priya: INT8 profile (aggressive): quantized more layers to INT8, added per-channel scaling, latency p50 120ms per token, total 10.5s, quality 0.86 — here you see bigger quality delta on some prompt classes.
[04:25] Samir: that 6 point drop sounds like a lot for our summarization use case. which prompts were sensitive?
[04:32] Priya: the failure modes were mostly detailed factual recall and entity formatting (dates/IDs) — INT8 sometimes changes rare token probabilities. For short prompts with looser fidelity it's often fine.

[04:50] Dana: can Optimize recommend mixed profiles per-route? we have multiple endpoints with different SLAs.
[04:56] Priya: yes that's the point — Optimize suggests per-route profiles. In the console you can create traffic rules: e.g., route /summarize -> use FP8 conservative profile; route /chat-fast -> INT8 aggressive. We also surface recommended batch sizes and cache TTLs.

[05:20] Alex: and on Dedicated you get predictable throughput so you can pick more aggressive INT8 to hit cost targets; on Hosted we can still do INT8 but the fallback and rollout policies are helpful to protect quality.

[05:35] Marta: what's the impact of KV cache on quantization quality? we heavily use prefix-caching.
[05:40] Priya: KV cache doesn't change quantization math, but it can change effective latency: because using cached KV reduces compute per-token, the relative benefit of INT8 shrinks if most tokens are from cache. Also for very long context runs, quantization error can accumulate subtly — our evals include long-context prompts to surface regressions.

[06:05] [06:05] Priya: switching to Optimize UI — here's the quality vs latency scatter plot. X axis latency, Y axis automated quality metric (higher better). Each dot is a profile. you can filter by model family, sequence length, and hardware. We flag profiles with statistically significant regressions.

[06:30] Samir: how do you compute the quality metric? we have proprietary scoring for our use case.
[06:35] Priya: we support custom eval harnesses — you upload your prompt set and label/metric; Optimize runs profiles and compares. By default we calculate a composite of ROUGE/BLEU-like signals plus a hallucination detector. But you can plug in your own script.

[06:55] Alex: note on instrumentation — we capture token-level confidence and delta metrics so you can create alerts if a profile increases hallucination rate.

[07:05] Dana: security questions: SOC2, SSO, KMS — what do we get in Private?
[07:12] Alex: for Private/Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS, audit logs, SAML SSO, and VPC peering. We'll attach our security pack and SOC2 report — I'll share the link after.

[07:30] Marta: latency SLOs — can we get p95 below 120ms at 512 tokens?
[07:36] Alex: depends on model/hardware; with Dedicated on A100 or Blackwell and INT8 it's realistic; Optimize helps find config to meet SLOs while preserving quality by recommending batch sizes, kv cache TTLs, and quant profiles.

[07:50] [07:50] Priya: quick note on evaluation cadence — Optimize can run nightly regression checks across profiles; we can set thresholds to auto-fail a rollout if quality drops beyond X%.

[08:05] Samir: for the PoC we'd like: (1) run our prompt set across FP16/FP8/INT8; (2) measure p50/p95 single-shot and throughput with typical batch patterns; (3) have Redwood recommend per-route profile and a rollout plan.

[08:20] Priya: perfect, we typically do that. For scope, we'll need your prompt set and explicit acceptance criteria (like acceptable quality delta).

[08:35] Dana: timeline — can you deliver the initial benchmark within 4 business days?
[08:40] Alex: yes, assuming we get the prompt set by Monday we can turn around the benchmark and profiles within 3-4 business days.

[08:50] [08:50] Priya: demo note: we intentionally included both short and long prompts — here's an example where INT8 produced a truncated date format, FP8 preserved it. (reads example) — you can see differences in tokenization and probability mass for rare tokens.

[09:10] Samir: on hardware, what do you recommend: A100 vs H100 vs Blackwell?
[09:18] Priya: H100/Blackwell gives better kernel coverage for FP8/INT8 and often better speedups. A100 can still benefit but sometimes needs specific kernel fallbacks. For production Dedicated we'd advise H100 or later if FP8 is a key part of your strategy.

[09:35] Marta: cost model — how much cost saving if we move from FP16 to INT8?
[09:41] Alex: it depends on utilization and token distribution; approximate compute cost reduction around 30-50% factoring both memory and compute improvements and batching. We'll surface unit economics in the benchmark spreadsheet.

[09:55] Priya: switching to the UI again — here's how you create a staged rollout: create profile, run internal eval, create canary with 5% traffic, monitor quality and latency, then ramp to 25/50/100. If quality regresses, automatic rollback triggers.

[10:20] Samir: can we restrict rollouts to specific customer cohorts? we want to test with non-critical traffic only.

[10:25] Priya: yes you can route by header or account id; Redwood Console allows route-level targeting.

[10:35] [10:35] Dana: any gotchas with mixed-precision models? we're using a slightly modified Llama variant with adapter layers.

[10:42] Priya: adapter layers can be sensitive — Optimize will detect layers with high sensitivity and recommend keeping them in FP16/FP8. We can also do layer-wise profiling to propose hybrid quantization.

[11:00] Alex: quick interjection — competitors like Lambda are doing some of this but they don't have our integrated rollout/eval/alerting tied to production routes; Bedrock has managed endpoints but less transparent profiling guidance.

[11:12] [11:12] Priya: demo wrap-up — the high-level recommendation from the demo: route-sensitive profiles: use FP8-conservative for accuracy-critical routes, INT8-aggressive for cost-sensitive asynchronous jobs; run nightly regression checks and tie alerts to your acceptance metrics.

[11:35] Samir: sounds reasonable. we'll likely ask for a short window where we test INT8 on a small subset of traffic.

[11:45] Marta: SRE will want to see the latency and error budgets; can you include configuration for autoscaling in Dedicated?

[11:51] Alex: yes we'll include suggested autoscale policies (GPU pool sizes, burst policies) in the benchmark spreadsheet.

[12:05] Dana: one security follow-up — do you store prompt/response data for Optimize evals? we have strict residency rules.

[12:12] Priya: for Hosted, data used in Optimize runs can be redacted or you can bring your own evaluation runner in Private; we support on-prem eval execution if required. We'll call out data retention options in the security docs.

[12:30] [12:30] Priya: a quick note about evaluation noise: longer-context prompts have higher variance; we report confidence intervals and require multiple seeds to make statistical calls.

[12:48] Alex: ok let's capture next steps — we'll send the security pack, the quant guide, and the benchmark template. Priya will produce the demo recording clip and run the first PoC bench when you share the prompt set.

[13:05] Samir: one more question about observability — do you export traces to our Datadog?

[13:11] Alex: yes we support exporting metrics and traces via OTLP/Datadog integration; we'll include config snippets.

[13:25] Priya: meanwhile, if you want a quick taste: try our Optimize quickstart in the console; there's a sample profile you can run against a small prompt set.

[13:35] Dana: great, let's do that.

[13:40] [13:40] Alex: recap and next steps: 1) Samir provide prompt set and acceptance criteria by 2026-02-17; 2) Redwood (Alex/Priya) to run benchmark + share profiles and spreadsheet by 2026-02-18; 3) schedule PoC kickoff week of 2026-02-24. We'll also share security docs and SOC2 link.

[13:58] Marta: thanks all.

[14:02] Samir: thanks, talk soon.

[14:06] Alex: thanks, bye.

(Transcript note: occasional mis-hearings in proper nouns and acronyms; speaker labels may be approximate.)
